Pirathahini, Sathurshan — thank you for the chance to put this together. Everything here comes out of one MLS® pull run this week: every detached bungalow sold within 1.5 kilometres of your door since August 1, and every one currently for sale. Two things came out of it that change the usual answer, and both are in here. There is also a tax question on this sale that is worth more than any staging decision, and I have flagged it rather than guessed at it — I am a CPA as well as your agent, and that part we can do properly.

Section 01 · The property

The largest house in the comparison — by a clear margin — with a renovated main floor and a second suite below.

1062 Midland Avenue is a detached bungalow built in 1960 on the west side of Midland between Lawrence and Eglinton, in Bendale. It carries 1,460 sq ft above grade on a 49 × 117 ft lot, with three bedrooms and a renovated five-piece bath up, a fourth bedroom and a second kitchen below, an attached garage and a private double drive. The main floor has been taken back to new: white shaker kitchen with quartz and stainless, hardwood throughout, pot lights, crown moulding, California shutters, and a sunken primary with a walk-out to the yard and a walk-in closet the size of a small bedroom. Outside there is a covered cabana and an interlock patio.

The 2020 transfer is the one piece of history that carries real money, and it is not a pricing question — it is a tax question. Title shows $960,000, but a parent-to-child transfer is not an arm's-length sale, so the figure written on the deed is not what governs. For tax purposes the cost base is the fair market value of the property on the day it changed hands in July 2020, whatever number appeared on the paperwork.

That matters because today's evidence puts the house below that level. Establishing the July 2020 value properly — and confirming how the property has been reported since — is the first thing we should do, ahead of any decision about price or timing. Section 12 sets out why.

SYNERGY's own MLS® extract, January–September 2026: 52 detached bungalow sales in Bendale, 242 across Bendale, Ionview, Dorset Park, Kennedy Park, Eglinton East, Clairlea-Birchmount, Woburn and Scarborough Village. GTA figure from TRREB Market Watch, September 2026.

Two markets are running at once. Across the Greater Toronto Area, TRREB reported 5,040 sales in September against 5,592 a year earlier, with the average price down 5.0% to $1,006,409 and detached homes down 4.9%. New listings fell 14.3%. Buyers at the top of the market are waiting.

The detached bungalow market in south Scarborough did not follow. Across 242 sales this year the average was 98.9% of list and 28% — more than one in four — sold above the asking price. In Bendale specifically, 52 sales at a median of $875,000 and 98.2% of list. This is where the buyers who have been priced out of the $1.2M Toronto detached median actually are, and the depth of that demand is the single best thing your sale has going for it.

What it does not mean is that anything sells. The seventeen sales nearest you this autumn ranged from $716,000 to $950,000 for homes of broadly similar size, and the spread was not about size at all. Sections 4 and 5 show what it was about.

Section 04 · The comparable sales

Seventeen bungalow sales within 1.5 km. Size barely moved the price — condition moved it $187,000.

The search covered every detached bungalow sold within 1.5 kilometres since August 1, with three or more bedrooms and two or more bathrooms. Seventeen came back. Because the MLS® sheets carry exact above-grade floor area rather than a range, we can do something a normal CMA cannot: hold size constant and watch what else moves.

What moves is condition, then a garage. Two sales make it plain. 49 Kilgreggan Crescent — 1,300 sq ft, entirely original, pink walls and a wood-panelled basement — sold for $743,000. 47 Haileybury Drive — 1,200 sq ft, so a hundred feet smaller, but fully renovated, staged and with an attached garage — sold for $930,000. Same box, same pocket, same autumn. A $187,000 gap.

Your house is 1,460 sq ft, renovated, with an attached garage and a double drive. On this evidence it belongs at the Haileybury end. Section 5 works through what pulls it back.

Section 05 · What the numbers actually say

Price per square foot runs backwards here — and that is the trap.

Across the fifteen sales that reported a floor area, the rate ranged from $572 to $914 per square foot. It runs inversely with size, because in a bungalow pocket the land carries most of the value and the house carries the rest. The smallest home in the set, 3 Century Drive at 1,017 sq ft, fetched the highest rate. The largest, 49 Kilgreggan at 1,300 sq ft, fetched the lowest.

Which means the obvious arithmetic — median rate of $737 multiplied by your 1,460 sq ft — produces $1,076,000, and that number is worthless. Any CMA that leads with a price per square foot on a set like this is reading the data backwards. The right comparison is to the largest homes in the set and to the ones in your condition, and that is what Section 6 does.

Before the number: this is built from data, not from a visit. Every figure here comes from MLS® records, MPAC, Teranet and the photographs on each listing. Nobody has been inside 1062 Midland — the renovation photographs are from February 2024 and the house has been tenanted since. A walkthrough can move this range in either direction, and that is the next step rather than an afterthought.

With that said, here is where the evidence sits. Take the road out of it and this house belongs above 47 Haileybury: 260 sq ft larger, the same attached garage, finishes at the same level, and a second kitchen Haileybury does not have. At 1,460 sq ft above grade it is the largest home in the set of seventeen, and the nearest is 1,368.

The road is what brings it back, and the evidence there is one-directional. The highest sale on an arterial in this entire search is $860,000 — one sale, 764 Brimley, and it took sixty-nine days at 93% of list. Every arterial home currently for sale is sitting: 1074 Midland at eighty-six days, 712 Brimley at forty-nine, 1008 Kennedy at twenty-eight, 812 Kennedy at two hundred and nineteen. Side streets, over the same period, sold at 98.5% of list in a median of twenty-two days.

Fair warning on that comparison: a single sale is thin evidence, and 764 Brimley was in original condition, so it was never going to test $900,000. Your house is a different proposition. But the five active listings point the same way as the one sale, and that consistency is what sets the range.

Netting it out: $895,000 to $925,000, with $910,000 the honest midpoint. At $910,000 the house prices at $623 per square foot — below the $643 that 18 Romulus achieved in original condition with no garage at all. That is the test to apply to any number anyone puts in front of you, including this one. A house this size, this finished, should not be priced near the rate an untouched one fetched.

Section 10 · Who buys a home like yours

Three buyers — and the vacant basement decides which one shows up.

Eight of the seventeen comparable sales had a second kitchen or a basement apartment, and as a group they sold at 98.8% of list against 97.7% for the rest. The suite is not a large premium in dollars. What it does is widen the buyer pool, and in a thinner market that is worth more than the premium.

The multi-generational family

The most likely buyer and the one who pays most. Three bedrooms and a renovated bath upstairs, a fourth bedroom and a full kitchen downstairs behind a separate entrance. They are buying the layout and the fact that the work is already done — this family does not want a project, and your main floor means they do not have one. The attached garage and double drive matter to them more than to anyone else.

The investor

For this buyer, a main road is close to irrelevant and the two units are the entire proposition. The main floor leased at $3,150 furnished in 2024 and the lower unit is vacant from November 15, which means they can set the lower rent at today's market rather than inheriting one. Expect them to bid early and firmly, and rarely to be the top bid against a family — but they are the floor under the price and the reason this house will not sit.

The first-time buyer priced out of a side street

A renovated detached bungalow with a garage, 1,460 sq ft, under $875,000 is a rare thing in E09 right now — the Bendale median is $875,000 and most of what trades there is smaller or original. Midland is the trade-off they make to get the house, and some of them will make it happily. They are the volume at an open house even when they are not the buyer.

Section 12 · The part worth more than the staging

This sale may produce a deductible loss. Whether it does depends on four answers.

I am a Chartered Professional Accountant as well as your agent, so I am going to be direct about this: the tax position on 1062 Midland is worth more money than any decision we make about price or presentation, and it is the one part of this sale that cannot be fixed afterwards. What follows is a set of flags, not advice — but each one is work our in-house practice can do as part of the listing rather than as a separate engagement billed later.

The 2020 transfer was not an arm's-length sale, so the number on title is not your costTitle shows $960,000 for the July 2020 transfer, but a parent-to-child transfer is a non-arm's-length transaction. In that situation the tax rules set the acquiring party's cost at the fair market value of the property on the day it transferred, regardless of what consideration was actually recorded. So the first question is not what the deed says — it is what 1062 Midland was genuinely worth in July 2020. That figure needs to be established and supported before this house sells, not after, because the evidence to support it gets harder to assemble as time passes.
If there is a loss, the rental history is what makes it usableToday's evidence puts the house below the level the 2020 title figure implies. A loss on real property held to earn rental income is generally an allowable capital loss: it can be carried back against capital gains in the three preceding years, or carried forward indefinitely. A loss on a property that was personal-use — a home the family lived in — is denied outright and simply disappears. Your property has been tenanted, which is the side of that line you want to be on, but the characterization has to be supported by how it was actually used and reported, not by how we describe it now.
Whether capital cost allowance was ever claimedIf CCA was claimed against the building in any year it was rented, that changes the arithmetic on disposition and can produce recapture or a different treatment of the loss on the building portion. It is a yes-or-no question with a large dollar consequence, and the answer is in the returns that have already been filed. This is the single fastest thing to check and the one I would check first.
The other side of the 2020 transferA non-arm's-length transfer is a disposition for the person transferring as well. Whoever transferred the property in July 2020 had a deemed disposition at fair market value in that year, and if the property was not their principal residence for the whole period they owned it, that was a reportable event. Worth confirming it was handled, because an unreported family transfer has a way of surfacing when the property next changes hands and the Land Transfer Tax record is pulled.
And the tenancy, which is not a tax question but will shape the saleThe main floor is tenanted and the lower unit is vacant from November 15. Under the Residential Tenancies Act a buyer cannot simply take possession of the occupied unit — vacant possession has to be arranged before closing, either by agreement with the tenant or through the purchaser's own-use route, and the notice periods are not short. Selling with the tenancy in place is entirely workable and the investor buyer prefers it. It just narrows the pool, and we should decide which way we are going before the listing goes live rather than after an offer arrives.

How we help

Four questions, all answerable from documents you already have, and all of them worth settling before we talk about price again. Our in-house professionals flag what deserves a closer look before it becomes a costly mistake.

Flags for discussion, not legal or tax advice, and not a determination of your tax position. Marshall Accounting and Tax Advisory can review your specific circumstances and the returns as filed, and a lawyer should review anything touching the tenancy.

Questions sellers ask

The things most people want to ask, answered before you have to.

Being on Midland — how much is that really costing us?

Less than you would think, and it is measurable rather than a feeling. The one other main-road sale in the search, 764 Brimley, reached $860,000 — but it needed sixty-nine days and gave up 7% of its ask to get there, against a 22-day, 98% norm off the arterials. So the road costs time and negotiating room more than it costs headline price, and the way to manage both is a list price that does not ask buyers to overlook it.

Why list at $929,000 when the neighbour is asking $899,000?

Because they are not the same house. 1074 Midland is 1,170 sq ft above grade against your 1,460 — a quarter smaller, unrenovated and showing empty — on an almost identical lot. It opened at $929,000, came down to $899,000 and has still not sold, which tells us about that house rather than about yours. The figure that matters is the rate: at $929,000 you are asking $636 per square foot, less than the $643 an original-condition bungalow with no garage achieved on a nearby street. We are not asking for a premium, we are asking for the size and the finish.

Could it be worth more than this?

It could, and the walkthrough is what will tell us. Everything in this document was built from records and photographs — nobody has been inside. If the house presents today the way it did in the 2024 photographs, there is a case for going higher. If two years of tenancy have taken a toll, this range is already right. That is exactly why we look before we list rather than after.

Does being on Midland really cost us?

It costs time more than price, and the evidence is specific. The highest price any home on an arterial has sold for in this search is $860,000, and it needed sixty-nine days at 93% of list. Four of the five main-road homes currently for sale are stale. Off the arterials, the same period produced 98.5% of list in a median of twenty-two days. Your size and finish are the answer to that — but the list price has to respect it rather than argue with it.

Should we renovate anything else first?

No. Your main floor is the reason this house is worth what it is — the comparable sales show a $187,000 gap between renovated and original at the same size, and you are already on the right side of it. Paint touch-ups, decluttering and staging are the only spend worth making, and they are included at the Signature level.

Does the tenant have to leave before we sell?

No, and there is a real argument for keeping them. The investor buyer prefers a tenanted main floor with the lower unit vacant from November 15, because they can set the lower rent at today's market. A family buyer needs vacant possession, which the Residential Tenancies Act requires us to arrange before closing. We should pick a lane before going live, and our legal counsel walks you through either one.

Our basement unit — is the retrofit status a problem?

It is a disclosure item, not a deal-breaker. Four of the nineteen current listings in this radius carry the same caveat word for word, including 22 Arnprior at $998,000. What matters is that we say it plainly up front and price accordingly, so it never becomes a renegotiation during a conditional period.

What if it doesn't sell?

Then we adjust on evidence, not nerves. You get showing and traffic data weekly, and we agree in advance what a slow first two weeks means. The live links in Sections 4 and 8 stay current, so you can see the same market I am seeing between conversations rather than waiting for me to tell you.

How long does it actually take?

About two weeks of preparation from the decision to list, then a firm sale typically in thirty to sixty days. The median across the comparable sales was twenty-two days. Closing is usually thirty to ninety days after that, and the date is negotiable to suit you.

What will we actually walk away with?

Use the slider in Section 9 — those are your real numbers at any price, and with no mortgage to discharge the net figure is close to what lands. What it does not show is the tax outcome, which is Section 12 and is the larger number of the two.

Do we pay anything if it doesn't sell?

No. Commission is earned on a completed sale, and staging, painting and photography are ours to carry in both packages.

What happens with our taxes?

That is the question most agents cannot answer, and on this property it is worth more than the staging. The 2020 parent-to-child transfer means your cost base is the July 2020 fair market value rather than the figure on title, and if that produces a loss, the rental history is what determines whether it is usable. Section 12 sets out all four questions. I handle that part myself.

Who will we actually be dealing with?

Me, from the first conversation through closing and through the return that follows it. Behind me is a five-agent team plus in-house legal and accounting, so nothing waits on one calendar — but you are never handed off.

What if we change our minds?

Tell me. We would rather pause a listing than push a family into a sale they are not ready for. This business was built on families who came back and who sent their relatives.

What happens next

A walkthrough first — then you decide whether a sale is the right move at all.

Nothing in this document commits you to anything, and the order of what follows matters. Everything to this point was built from records and photographs. The next step is to see the house, confirm the range against what is actually there today, and talk it through together. Only after that is there a conversation worth having about whether selling serves you.

Step one · read it overTake your time with this. Mark up anything you disagree with — every figure has a source and the two live links let you check the market yourself. Then call or email whenever it suits you and we will go through it together, as long as you want to.
Step two · the walkthroughHalf an hour at the house. This is what confirms the valuation: the renovation photographs are from February 2024 and the house has been tenanted since, so the condition today is the one variable that can move the range meaningfully in either direction. Bring any questions the document raised.
Step three · the two documentsWhatever you decide about selling, two things are worth settling: what was recorded on the July 2020 transfer, and whether capital cost allowance has ever been claimed against the building. Those answers drive Section 12, and they matter whether you sell this year, next year, or not at all.
Step four · decide, togetherIf, having seen the numbers and walked the house, you believe a sale is in your best interest, we are glad to explore it with you and to map out what it would look like. If the answer is to hold, or to wait for spring, or to keep it tenanted — that is a perfectly good answer and we will say so.

If you do decide to proceed, what follows is roughly two weeks of preparation — painting, staging, professional photography, floor plans, drone and a twilight exterior — then live on MLS® with the ad campaign starting the same day, weekly traffic and feedback data, and the tax work handled in-house at closing. We would walk you through all of it before anything is signed.

When you're ready

Read it over, then let's talk it through.

There is no decision to make today. Take as long as you need with this, and when you have had a chance to go through it, get in touch and we will walk the house together and confirm whether the numbers here hold up in person. If a sale turns out to be the right move for you, we would be glad to explore it together — and if it does not, you will still have a clear picture of what you own and what it is worth. Either way, the questions in Section 12 are worth answering, and we are happy to help with those whatever you decide.
